articles.title: Reclaim the terminal
articles.summary: The terminal is not always the same, even when a program is piping input to it. The terminal's fd 0 and fd 1 are connected to different processes, and the shell only launches the whole pipeline at once. This means that each stage of the pipeline can read from its own stdin, and the next stage can start reading from the previous stage's pipe. This is possible because the binary itself is piping input to itself, and the shell only needs to know which stage is currently reading from stdin.

articles.title: Sing-song: a speakable encoding for long numbers and keys
articles.summary: This is a fun experiment that started as a way to generate deterministic "usernames" for Nostr npub keys. The result is not as good as I'd want it to be, but it's not bad either, and it's not bad enough to be discarded. Sing-song: speakable encodings for long numbers and keys is a reversible encoding of arbitrary byte strings as pronounceable CV syllables. Its 64-syllable alphabet maps each 6-bit value directly to one syllable, and complete encodings preserve byte length and leading zero bytes, requiring no external length metadata.
